newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST- Irish 1997 GNP growth seen at five pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Irish 1997 GNP growth seen at five pct.

text.p: The Irish economy is expected to record real GNP growth of about five percent in 1997 as rising export volumes offset a deceleration in domestic demand, an Irish thinktank said on Friday.

"Although, as always, some uncertainties remain, it seems highly probable that in 1997 Ireland will again record a growth rate which is far above the European norm," Ireland's Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) said in a quarterly review.

"Our present forecast is for an increase of about five percent in real GNP, accompanied by a rise in consumer prices of around two percent, approximate stability in the Exchequer Borrowing Requirement and a modest recovery in the current account balance of payments surplus," the ESRI said.
It expects total visible exports to increase by about 11.5 percent in volume and 12.25 percent in value as the European economy shows a moderate upturn.
This should make up for a deceleration in personal consumption which the ESRI expects to slow to 6.2 percent in 1997 after a forecast increase of 8.2 percent in 1996.
With economic growth expected to be slightly slower than in 1995, the increase in total employment is expected to be smaller than in the two previous years, the review said.
The ESRI is expecting the number of those in work to rise by about 2.5 percent or 33,000.
The review said that the course of Irish interest rates in 1997 would depend mainly on external factors, particularly market perceptions of the likelihood of EMU proceeding on its planned time scale.

"On balance, it seems most likely that some uncertainty will remain for most of the year before it finally becomes clear that EMU will proceed on schedule. On this assumption, little change is forecast in Irish interest rates, short or long term, in 1997," the ESRI said.
